Homo Naledi - Cave of the Rising Star

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A new extra ordinary discovery in the cradle of mankind has international scientists in a spin

Summary:
A new discovery - the single largest fossil hominin find yet made on the continent of Africa. The initial discovery was made in 2013 in a cave known as Rising Star in the Cradle of Humankind World Heritage Site, some 50 kilometers (30 miles) northwest of Johannesburg, South Africa, by Wits University scientists and volunteer cavers.

The unusual combination of characters that we see in the Homo naledi skulls and skeletons is unlike anything that we have seen in any other early hominin species.

The fossils lay in a chamber about 90 meters (some 100 yards) from the cave entrance, accessible only through a chute so narrow that a special team of very slender individuals was needed to retrieve them.


Further information:
So far the team has recovered parts of at least 15 individuals of the same species, a small fraction of the fossils believed to remain in the chamber. “With almost every bone in the body represented multiple times, Homo naledi is already practically the best-known fossil member of our lineage,” said team leader Lee Berger, research professor in the Evolutionary Studies Institute at the University of the Witwatersrand and a National Geographic Explorer-in-Residence, who led the two expeditions that discovered and recovered the fossils.

"This is a tremendously significant find," said Terry Garcia, Chief Science and Exploration Officer of the National Geographic Society. "That is why when National Geographic received a call from Lee Berger reporting the fossils' initial discovery, we immediately committed our support to this remarkable effort."

H. naledi was named after the Rising Star cave — “naledi” means “star” in the local Sesotho language. “Overall, Homo naledi looks like one of the most primitive members of our genus, but it also has some surprisingly human-like features, enough to warrant placing it in the genus Homo,” said John Hawks of the University of Wisconsin, Madison, U.S., a senior author on the paper describing the new species. “H. naledi had a tiny brain, about the size of an average orange (about 500 cubic centimeters), perched atop a very slender body.” The research shows that an average H. naledi stood approximately 1.5 meters (about 5 feet) tall and weighed about 45 kg (almost 100 pounds).
In the initial expedition, over a period of 21 days more than 60 cavers and scientists worked together in what Marina Elliott, one of the excavating scientists, described as “some of the most difficult and dangerous conditions ever encountered in the search for human origins.” Elliott was one of six women selected as “underground astronauts” from a global pool of candidates after Berger issued a call on social media for experienced scientist/cavers who could fit through the 18cm-wide (7-inch) cave opening. Social media continued to play a role in the project, as the team shared expedition progress with a large public audience, schoolchildren and scientists. “This was a first in the history of the field,” said Hawks, who worked with Berger to design the media outreach.

The fossils were analyzed in a unique workshop in May 2014, funded by the South African NRF, Wits University and National Geographic. More than 50 experienced scientists and early-career researchers came together to study and analyze the treasure trove of fossils and compose scientific papers.

Much remains to be discovered in the Rising Star cave. “This chamber has not given up all of its secrets,” Berger said. “There are potentially hundreds if not thousands of remains of H. naledi still down there.”

Wits owns and manages important fossil sites in the Cradle, and for nearly 80 years its scientists have made some of the most extraordinary fossil finds here.

Press Release:


Secrets of the Rising Star Cave
On a Friday evening in 2013, two extreme cavers found themselves deep below ground in the Cradle of Humankind. Coming across a narrow crack in the cave floor, they descended down a twelve metre shaft and emerged into a chamber only to discover ancient bones. Carte Blanche reports on the extraordinary scientific discovery of a new species of human relative - Homo Naledi.


Script:


Cave of the Rising star FINAL SCRIPT DEREK VO.

Commentary One
Since 2008 the stars have aligned for Professor Lee Berger.
Exploring at the time, near Malapa cave, with his young son, Mathew tripped over a log and found a fossil. That would lead to the discovery of Australopithecus Sediba – a two million year old hominid

Professor Lee Berger
We had 5 years of the most remarkable science that anyone can ever participate in and I suddenly realized we had accomplished all our science epiphany I hadn’t been exploring since that moment when Mathew had shown me that fossil.

Derek link
By 2013 after the excitement of Sediba had died down Lee knew that he wanted to get underground again. As luck would have it an amateur caver whom he had known for years suddenly pitched up at his office.

Lee
We had caved together looked for fossils together and he wanted back in and it was just that perfect moment

Commentary Two
Pedro Boshoff, geologist, maverick and caver had lost all his savings in the Congo

PEDRO
I asked him frankly Lee I need work please-And he told me look I will give you a temp job, go through all the caves you know and see if you can find something interesting

Lee
But I put one caveat on it – lets start in the places we know best
Derek
Your own backyard
Lee
My own backyard – because we had learnt a bit from Malapa – that was one kilometer from where I had spent 17 years looking

Commentary Three
Lee had noted around six hundred fossil sites, before Sediba had interrupted further exploration, and these were the caves Pedro started on. But there were just too many, so he roped in cavers, Rick Hunter and Steven Tucker

Steve
Back in 2013 we weren’t really thinking about fossil discoveries until Pedro asked us to keep an eye out for fossils


Pedro
Rick and Steve are extraordinary cavers, they can squeeze through impossible things, so they were pushing the extremities of the system

DEREK LINK
Keep your eyes on the ground not just the starry heavens and that is exactly as it happened

Commentary Four
On the evening of Friday the 13th, September 2013, Rick and Steve were filming in a cave they knew really well – Dineledi cave- or the cave of the Rising star

Rick
I was filming the area with my go pro trying to get nice images of the stalactites and where there was a nice section, Steven was in the way so he decided to crawl through a gap in floor and he saw it actually went down further

Commentary Five
Curious, Steve and Rick squirmed through the dark, narrow crack less than 18 cm wide. Since described like crawling down a narrow sharp intestine for 12 meters

Steve
I thought I had found everything there was to be found in the cave until this Friday night when dropping down this tiny crack we stumbled across a couple of bones on the floor

Commentary Six
But they couldn’t take any photo’s, their go pro was flat and so on Pedro’s instruction they returned – and then they showed him their first visuals.

PEDRO
I immediately knew!
What was your reaction?
I went ballistic …you could clearly see and several long bones

Commentary Seven
Unable to contain their excitement, they tried calling Lee, but he didn’t answer so they drove across town to his house.

Derek
Late one night Lee, a ring on the doorbell
Lee
I answer and there was a voice that said: “you are going to want to let us in! It’s Pedro. Pedro comes in with this amateur caver Steve Tucker, flips open a laptop and I saw something I never thought I would see in all my life-there was the mandible of a primitive hominid just lying on the ground in a cave
Derek
What was your first thought?
Lee
I cant probably repeat what my first thought was! My second thought was this is impossible- the next picture just as impossible a skull embedded in dirt. The third picture bones of what looked like a body…and then I couldn’t sleep.

Commentary eight
By 2am Lee decided to send the pictures to National Geographic’s Terry Garcia.

Lee
I said if you ever going to believe in me believe in me right now and that is explorer speak for I need money.
Derek
Just on the basis of a pic
Lee
And he said do what you need to do

Commentary nine
But then Lee got cold feet, so he taught Mathew how to use a scientific camera and once again they went back to the cave with Rick and Steve to confirm the find. Lee wouldn’t fit so he sent Mathew, now a teenager, down the narrow shaft

Matthew
I had never been properly caving before. I thought it was like Sterkfontein
Derek
Just bending slightly
Matthew
Just bending slightly! I was completely wrong!

LEE
And it is horrendous it takes 45 minutes of tiny squeezes before climbing up this thing called dragons back and there you stare into the abyss of a crack that wide

Matthew
I looked at this hole and was completely shocked it literally looked as if there was no hole there –I was stuck at this angle …and at the very bottom there is a meter drop … I looked at this in awe and knew what this was going to be.

Lee
45 minutes later I hear scrabbling and up pops Matthew’s head and because I am going for father of the year I didn’t go: “Are you ok? I went AND!
And I looked at those pictures and I pushed the button for go.

Commentary ten
Now Lee had to find skinny scientists in a hurry. Not knowing where he would source them, he put out a request on Facebook

Lee
I need skinny scientists who can work in a cave, who are willing to drop everything, and be here in three weeks, and work for a month for free – I didn’t tell them what it was

Commentary eleven
Canadian, Marina Elliot was three quarters of the way through her PHD. She is a climber, a caver and has a string of relevant degrees

Marina
And I read it and I thought oh my god that is me. I have to try this

Commentary twelve
Four weeks after Steve first dropped down into the Dinaledi chamber, Lee had people from all over the world camped outside the cave

Rick
We ran 3.5 kilometers of cable into the cave and had cameras set up so we could have a phone conversation through the cave

Steve
Most of the time lee was sitting in the command centre phone in hand ready to jump to action if anything does go wrong!

Commentary Thirteen
Also on site, were Lee’s six skinny scientists who became known as the underground astronauts. The first time Marina saw the 18 cm crack she was apprehensive

Marina
They took us to the top of the shoot and I thought oh mercy I am not sure I am prepared for this because it looked really bad

Commentary fourteen
For 21 days the astronauts made the journey down the shaft

Up sound girls in cave falling

It was uncomfortable and dangerous. These are Marina’s cell phone photos taken over a period of days.

Lee Up sound

That’s it!

Commentary Fifteen
While the underground astronauts sifted through a metre by a metre square on the chamber floor. Above ground the scientists were beginning to realize this was a huge find

Derek to Lee
Lee, a huge amount of material coming out of that cave
Lee
By the end of the first week, we had discovered more primitive hominid material than had been discovered in the richest site in the world, Sterkfontein in all of its decades of work

Commentary Seventeen
The vault at Wits became a hub of activity as Lee’s super team of local and international scientists interrogated the find

Lee
By the end of the 21 days we had more numbered fossils than had been discovered in the entire history of work in all of southern Africa

Commentary Sixteen
In the end 15 skeletons of different ages were found. That led to the teams most controversial announcement. Steve and Rick had stumbled onto a primitive burial chamber

Steve
As cavers we are particularly interested in how they got there – if we struggle today with lights and helmets how did something else get there

Commentary Seventeen
By Friday this week, other scientists had already questioned the burial hypothesis

Lee
You can imagine that a group of scientists are not going to say this lightly/
We have worked through all the probable and I guess as Sherlock holmes says you are left with the improbable and that is that we have found another species which clearly contemplated their own mortality ….and placed them in a remote chamber where nothing else could reach them ever until we did.

Commentary eighteen
Using technology they scanned, they printed and they shared with the public the story of Rising Star. But it was only this week – after two years of intensive investigation that they made the announcement of their findings to the world.

Up sound Lee
Ladies and gentleman I give you a new species of human ancestor homo Naledi

Derek
Lets chat about the star of the show

Professor Lee Berger
From the neck down its bizarre – the shoulders are like an ape the arm and hand become more and more human like and you would think it is a human hand but it isn’t because the fingers are curved – as much as any that we have discovered / The centre of the body everything is primitive…you have got primitive thorax and pine and flared pelvis but from mid thigh downwards it become completely human

Commentary Twenty
In a sneak preview ahead of the announcement I met Homo Naledi face to face

Lee
New species not behind armoured glass
Hand and feet of new species of early human ancestor – here a mandible
Derek
They could be a million years old
We don’t know
Could be a million years old could be 5 million
How can you not love your own ancestor


THE END


In at 00 01 00 00 00
Out at 00 14 02 00 00
Duration 13 02

PROMO ONE: 15 seconds
A huge discovery begins with two extreme cavers on a Friday night
Pedro
Rick and Steve are extraordinary cavers- they can squeeze through impossible things

PROMO TWO
I come face to face with Homo Naledi – new species of distant relative
Lee
Look at those teeth probably better than
Most complete hand ever found in human history
You make old bones sound sexy
It is sexy! How can you not love your own ancestor!

PROMO THREE 10 seconds
Why did Professor Lee Berger send his son into a dangerous cave?
Lee
And because I am going for father of the year I didn’t go: “Are you ok? I went AND!

LEE And it is horrendous it takes 45 minutes of tiny squeezes before climbing up this thing called dragons back and there you stare into the abyss of a crack that wide Matthew I looked at this hole and was completely shocked it literally looked as if there was no hole there –I was stuck at this angle …and at the very bottom there is a meter drop … I looked at this in awe and knew what this was going to be. Lee 45 minutes later I hear scrabbling and up pops Matthew’s head and because I am going for father of the year I didn’t go: “Are you ok? I went AND! And I looked at those pictures and I pushed the button for go. Commentary ten Now Lee had to find skinny scientists in a hurry. Not knowing where he would source them, he put out a request on Facebook Lee I need skinny scientists who can work in a cave, who are willing to drop everything, and be here in three weeks, and work for a month for free – I didn’t tell them what it was Commentary eleven Canadian, Marina Elliot was three quarters of the way through her PHD. She is a climber, a caver and has a string of relevant degrees Marina And I read it and I thought oh my god that is me. I have to try this Commentary twelve Four weeks after Steve first dropped down into the Dinaledi chamber, Lee had people from all over the world camped outside the cave Rick We ran 3.5 kilometers of cable into the cave and had cameras set up so we could have a phone conversation through the cave Steve Most of the time lee was sitting in the command centre phone in hand ready to jump to action if anything does go wrong! Commentary Thirteen Also on site, were Lee’s six skinny scientists who became known as the underground astronauts. The first time Marina saw the 18 cm crack she was apprehensive Marina They took us to the top of the shoot and I thought oh mercy I am not sure I am prepared for this because it looked really bad Commentary fourteen For 21 days the astronauts made the journey down the shaft Up sound girls in cave falling It was uncomfortable and dangerous. These are Marina’s cell phone photos taken over a period of days. Lee Up sound That’s it! Commentary Fifteen While the underground astronauts sifted through a metre by a metre square on the chamber floor. Above ground the scientists were beginning to realize this was a huge find Derek to Lee Lee, a huge amount of material coming out of that cave Lee By the end of the first week, we had discovered more primitive hominid material than had been discovered in the richest site in the world, Sterkfontein in all of its decades of work Commentary Seventeen The vault at Wits became a hub of activity as Lee’s super team of local and international scientists interrogated the find Lee By the end of the 21 days we had more numbered fossils than had been discovered in the entire history of work in all of southern Africa Commentary Sixteen In the end 15 skeletons of different ages were found. That led to the teams most controversial announcement. Steve and Rick had stumbled onto a primitive burial chamber Steve As cavers we are particularly interested in how they got there – if we struggle today with lights and helmets how did something else get there Commentary Seventeen By Friday this week, other scientists had already questioned the burial hypothesis Lee You can imagine that a group of scientists are not going to say this lightly/ We have worked through all the probable and I guess as Sherlock holmes says you are left with the improbable and that is that we have found another species which clearly contemplated their own mortality ….and placed them in a remote chamber where nothing else could reach them ever until we did. Commentary eighteen Using technology they scanned, they printed and they shared with the public the story of Rising Star. But it was only this week – after two years of intensive investigation that they made the announcement of their findings to the world. Up sound Lee Ladies and gentleman I give you a new species of human ancestor homo Naledi Derek Lets chat about the star of the show Professor Lee Berger From the neck down its bizarre – the shoulders are like an ape the arm and hand become more and more human like and you would think it is a human hand but it isn’t because the fingers are curved – as much as any that we have discovered / The centre of the body everything is primitive…you have got primitive thorax and pine and flared pelvis but from mid thigh downwards it become completely human Commentary Twenty In a sneak preview ahead of the announcement I met Homo Naledi face to face Lee New species not behind armoured glass Hand and feet of new species of early human ancestor – here a mandible Derek They could be a million years old We don’t know Could be a million years old could be 5 million How can you not love your own ancestor THE END In at 00 01 00 00 00 Out at 00 14 02 00 00 Duration 13 02 PROMO ONE: 15 seconds A huge discovery begins with two extreme cavers on a Friday night Pedro Rick and Steve are extraordinary cavers- they can squeeze through impossible things PROMO TWO I come face to face with Homo Naledi – new species of distant relative Lee Look at those teeth probably better than Most complete hand ever found in human history You make old bones sound sexy It is sexy! metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A new extra ordinary discovery in the cradle of mankind has international scientists in a spin
metadata.Summary: A new discovery - the single largest fossil hominin find yet made on the continent of Africa. The initial discovery was made in 2013 in a cave known as Rising Star in the Cradle of Humankind World Heritage Site, some 50 kilometers (30 miles) northwest of Johannesburg, South Africa, by Wits University scientists and volunteer cavers. The unusual combination of characters that we see in the Homo naledi skulls and skeletons is unlike anything that we have seen in any other early hominin species. The fossils lay in a chamber about 90 meters (some 100 yards) from the cave entrance, accessible only through a chute so narrow that a special team of very slender individuals was needed to retrieve them.
metadata.Further information: So far the team has recovered parts of at least 15 individuals of the same species, a small fraction of the fossils believed to remain in the chamber. “With almost every bone in the body represented multiple times, Homo naledi is already practically the best-known fossil member of our lineage,” said team leader Lee Berger, research professor in the Evolutionary Studies Institute at the University of the Witwatersrand and a National Geographic Explorer-in-Residence, who led the two expeditions that discovered and recovered the fossils. "This is a tremendously significant find," said Terry Garcia, Chief Science and Exploration Officer of the National Geographic Society. "That is why when National Geographic received a call from Lee Berger reporting the fossils' initial discovery, we immediately committed our support to this remarkable effort." H. naledi was named after the Rising Star cave — “naledi” means “star” in the local Sesotho language. “Overall, Homo naledi looks like one of the most primitive members of our genus, but it also has some surprisingly human-like features, enough to warrant placing it in the genus Homo,” said John Hawks of the University of Wisconsin, Madison, U.S., a senior author on the paper describing the new species. “H. naledi had a tiny brain, about the size of an average orange (about 500 cubic centimeters), perched atop a very slender body.” The research shows that an average H. naledi stood approximately 1.5 meters (about 5 feet) tall and weighed about 45 kg (almost 100 pounds). In the initial expedition, over a period of 21 days more than 60 cavers and scientists worked together in what Marina Elliott, one of the excavating scientists, described as “some of the most difficult and dangerous conditions ever encountered in the search for human origins.” Elliott was one of six women selected as “underground astronauts” from a global pool of candidates after Berger issued a call on social media for experienced scientist/cavers who could fit through the 18cm-wide (7-inch) cave opening. Social media continued to play a role in the project, as the team shared expedition progress with a large public audience, schoolchildren and scientists. “This was a first in the history of the field,” said Hawks, who worked with Berger to design the media outreach. The fossils were analyzed in a unique workshop in May 2014, funded by the South African NRF, Wits University and National Geographic. More than 50 experienced scientists and early-career researchers came together to study and analyze the treasure trove of fossils and compose scientific papers. Much remains to be discovered in the Rising Star cave. “This chamber has not given up all of its secrets,” Berger said. “There are potentially hundreds if not thousands of remains of H. naledi still down there.” Wits owns and manages important fossil sites in the Cradle, and for nearly 80 years its scientists have made some of the most extraordinary fossil finds here.
